A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices. The proof appendices can be matched across renumbering from v1 Appendices B–E to v2 Appendices C–F.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 3–5 report original synthetic sparse-logistic-regression experiments comparing single-layer and spindly models, including training dynamics and excess risk.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix B and Figure 6 add original simulations with power-law Gaussian covariance spectra.

M1.justification: The logistic objective, single-layer procedure, Hadamard parameterization w = u ⊙ v, gradient-flow dynamics, and early-stopping approach are unchanged. The added experiments vary the input distribution without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds anisotropic Gaussian input scenarios for the existing sparse-logistic task, with covariance-decay exponents 0.5 and 1.0 alongside an isotropic control. The preliminary Poisson and Exponential experiments mentioned in v1 are retained through relocation, not newly added.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison remains single-layer logistic regression versus the spindly parameterization, labeled Single and Spindle in new Figure 6. No additional comparator is evaluated; references to other algorithms remain discussion or future work.

E3.justification: The added experiment introduces a covariance-exponent sweep over 0, 0.5, and 1.0 and dimension sweeps extending to d = 500. The original Section 6 settings and Figure 5 sweep through d = 1000 remain unchanged. Appendix B does not establish whether its other experimental settings match Section 6.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests whether the performance gap survives departure from isotropic inputs and how dimension scaling responds to covariance decay. This adds a focused sensitivity analysis; the existing coordinate-dynamics analyses in Figures 3–4 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging Figure 5 over 10 independent dataset draws and display error bars. Figure 6 extends averaging and error-bar reporting to additional results without introducing a new uncertainty procedure or specifying additional run counts, seeds, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original Figures 3–5 are unchanged. New Figure 6 adds isotropic-control and anisotropic excess-risk curves: Single remains above Spindle, while its growth with dimension becomes sublinear under covariance decay. These are additional results, not established same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 5 refines the stated sparse-logistic minimax benchmark from O(s log d/n) to O(s log(ed/s)/n), distinguishing it from the retained method bound. The formal assumptions, propositions, theorems, and proof appendices otherwise remain unchanged after renumbering; no anisotropic bound is proved.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central separation between rotation-invariant and spindly algorithms. The conclusion adds the empirical claim that the gap persists for anisotropic inputs, explicitly leaving a corresponding theoretical lower bound open.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds an interpretation involving target–eigenspace alignment and reduced prediction-risk contributions from low-variance directions, and explains why the isotropic proof does not directly extend. Section 5 also qualifies the previous minimax-match description as matching up to logarithmic simplification.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies a new synthetic-input specification: Gaussian sampling with diagonal covariance and power-law eigenvalues, with exponent values identified in Figure 6. This is limited additional reproduction information; sample sizes, target construction, training settings, and repeat counts for that experiment are not separately specified.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Beck, Levi, and Bar-Sinai (2024) on grokking near linear separability. The sparse-recovery discussion is explicitly situated in the underdetermined regime and adds pointers to already-cited Warmuth et al. (2021). The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the conclusion and rate discussion, adds an Impact Statement, updates the publication footer, and moves the two existing open problems into new Appendix B. Subsequent appendices are renumbered; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel Figure 6 with covariance-dependent excess-risk curves. The existing spherical tangent-map diagram is relocated and renumbered from Figure 6 to Figure 7. Original experimental figures are retained, with otherwise limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added covariance-sensitivity experiment provides useful evidence beyond the original isotropic setting, while the conclusion clearly distinguishes that evidence from an unproved theoretical extension. Section 5 also qualifies the minimax comparison more precisely. These are modest gains: Appendix B leaves several reproduction settings unspecified, and the original proofs and experiments remain unchanged.
